facility_roles.note: The experiment ran in the Homestake Gold Mine, the mine in which the Sanford Underground Research Facility (facility:surf) was later built: SURF says it "is indelibly linked to the history of the Homestake Mine, which operated from 1876 until 2001." The Atlas has no separate record for the mine before SURF, so the host role points to facility:surf and the experiment starts before that facility's own dated intervals.
facility_roles.quote: The Homestake Solar Neutrino Observatory is located in the Homestake Gold Mine, at Lead, South Dakota

intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: Davis's Nobel lecture also shows the experiment's chamber half-excavated in the summer of 1965.
intervals.quote: The Homestake solar neutrino experiment was built in the period 1965–1967

intervals.label: operation
intervals.locator: Davis, Nobel Lecture 2002, p. 68, paragraph after Fig. 7; end: Davis, Nobel autobiography (Les Prix Nobel 2002), paragraph beginning 'I retired from Brookhaven in 1984'; SURF, Our Story
intervals.note: Start: the year Davis gives for the experiment becoming operational; the standard data set analysed by Cleveland et al. begins in 1970, when rise-time counting was introduced. End of operation: Davis writes that the experiment "continued to measure the solar neutrino flux until the late 1990s, when the Homestake Mine ceased operating"; SURF dates the end of the mine's operation to 2001, and Cleveland et al. (accepted October 1997) still describe the detector as measuring solar neutrinos. The date is therefore bounded between 1997 and 2001 and marked approximate; no source read gives the date of the last extraction. The standard data set of 108 observations ends in 1994, which is not the end of operation.
intervals.quote: The Homestake experiment became operational in 1967.

intervals.label: standard data set (rise-time counting)
intervals.locator: Cleveland et al. 1998, section 7.1; Davis, Nobel Lecture 2002, p. 72
intervals.note: Davis: "We began using this new system in 1970, and after about one year of observations, a clear neutrino signal was observed." The 1998 paper analyses 108 solar neutrino observations made between 1970 and 1994; it introduced rise-time counting in late 1970, starting with run 18.
intervals.quote: Our standard data set consists of 108 solar neutrino observations made between 1970 and 1994.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.locator: Davis, Nobel autobiography (Les Prix Nobel 2002), paragraph beginning 'I retired from Brookhaven in 1984'; SURF, Our Story, 'The Unique History of the Black Hills'
intervals.note: Davis: "The experiment continued to measure the solar neutrino flux until the late 1990s, when the Homestake Mine ceased operating." SURF says the mine operated until 2001, so the date is bounded between 1997 (Cleveland et al. still describe ongoing measurements) and 2001 and marked approximate. The standard data set of 108 observations ends in 1994, which is not the end of operation.
intervals.quote: The experiment continued to measure the solar neutrino flux until the late 1990s, when the Homestake Mine ceased operating.

quantity.locator: Davis, Nobel Lecture 2002, p. 66; Cleveland et al. 1998, section 3.1
quantity.note: The 380 m³ is a unit conversion of the 100,000-gallon figure (100,000 US gallons is 378.5 m³). Cleveland et al. 1998, section 3.1, give the fill as 615 metric tons of tetrachloroethylene in a horizontal steel tank 6.1 m in diameter and 14.6 m long.
quantity.quote: to build a 100,000-gallon chlorine-argon neutrino detector in the Homestake Gold Mine, in Lead, South Dakota

quantity.note: Depth stated in Raymond Davis Jr.'s Nobel lecture as the 4850-foot (1478 m) level of the Homestake mine (quote); this is the same 4850-foot level of the Homestake mine that facility:surf's 4850 Level (dedicated 2009, per that facility's own sourced interval) later reused, but the Davis chlorine tank's specific chamber within that level is not separately geolocated by any source consulted -- see the note on site placement.
quantity.quote: A large chamber and a smaller control room were excavated at the 4850-foot (1478 m) level of the mine.

name: Homestake chlorine experiment
notes: No distinct sourced coordinate for the Davis chlorine-tank chamber (as opposed to the mine/facility generally) was found, so no site record is created for it. `facility_roles` references the existing facility:surf (its own record carries the pre-SURF 'Homestake gold mine' interval and its site:surf-surface-campus point, a campus-grade point shown as approximate). This is NOT the same physical location as site:surf-4850-level-dune-far-detector (the DUNE far-detector cavern), which is deliberately not referenced here.

Dates: the experiment became operational in 1967 (Davis, Nobel Lecture) after construction in 1965-1967 (Cleveland et al. 1998). The 1998 paper's standard data set of 108 observations runs from 1970, when rise-time counting was introduced, to 1994, but operation did not stop then: Davis writes that the experiment continued until the late 1990s, when the Homestake Mine ceased operating, and SURF dates the end of the mine's operation to 2001. The end of operation is therefore bounded between 1997 and 2001 and marked approximate.

physics_goals.quote: The Homestake Solar Neutrino Detector, based on the inverse beta-decay reaction νe +37Cl →37Ar + e-, has been measuring the flux of solar neutrinos since 1970.
physics_goals.value: Detect solar neutrinos via the inverse beta-decay reaction on chlorine-37, converting it to argon-37

summary.plain: A tank of dry-cleaning fluid nearly a mile underground in a South Dakota gold mine, run for decades by Ray Davis, that made the first detection of solar neutrinos and found far fewer than expected: a puzzle that lasted until the turn of the century.
summary.technical: Radiochemical chlorine-argon solar-neutrino experiment in the Homestake Gold Mine, Lead, South Dakota, 1478 m (4850 ft) underground; 380 m³ (100,000 gal) perchloroethylene target. Built 1965-1967 and operational from 1967; the standard data set of 108 observations spans 1970-1994 and gives a 37Ar production rate of 2.56±0.16(stat)±0.16(syst) SNU, about one-third of the Standard Solar Model prediction -- the original 'solar neutrino problem', later resolved by neutrino oscillation (SNO, Super-Kamiokande).

unique_capabilities.locator: Nobel Committee for Physics, Advanced information on the Nobel Prize in Physics 2002, section "Neutrino astronomy"; Davis, Nobel autobiography (Les Prix Nobel 2002)
unique_capabilities.note: The Nobel Committee says Davis discovered solar neutrinos and that his measured fluxes were always below the calculated ones (the solar neutrino problem). Davis's Nobel autobiography gives the size of the deficit: 'a solar neutrino signal approximately one-third of the expected flux from the standard solar model calculated by John Bahcall'. 'First' is the reading of 'discovered'.
unique_capabilities.quote: Davis discovered solar neutrinos. Solar neutrino fluxes measured by him have always been below the calculated ones, this being known as the “solar neutrino problem”.
unique_capabilities.value: First experiment to detect solar neutrinos, and the one that revealed the 'solar neutrino problem' (a measured rate about one-third of the theoretical prediction)
